Welcome to the Southsea Infant School website.
Our Vision is of an inclusive, caring school community where every child is happy, will achieve their best, and become confident, ambitious, responsible and independent.
Through exceptional teaching, an engaging curriculum, strong relationships with families and by knowing our children really well as individuals, we aim to nurture a lifelong love of learning and a thirst for knowledge.
We hope that this website will answer many of your questions, but please feel free to contact us with any queries, and we will be happy to help.
If you would like to know more, please do not hesitate to get in touch to arrange a visit.
We look forward to meeting you.
Scroll down to the bottom of this page to view our calendar.
If you require paper copies of any of the information on our website, please contact admin@southsea.portsmouth.sch.uk.

Our Vision is of a caring school community where every child is happy, will achieve their best, become confident, ambitious, responsible and independent through exceptional teaching and by knowing our children really well as individuals, we will nurture a lifelong love of learning and a thirst for knowledge.
At Southsea Infant School we believe that all children have the right to feel safe, cared for and valued whilst receiving the very best education we can offer. Through our carefully selected values, we encourage our children to have the highest of aspirations for their future and support them to become lifelong learners. These values permeate our curriculum, extra curricular activities and compliment the caring ethos of our school.
We support children to keep trying even when they find things challenging. By doing this they build resilience so that they can manage when they make mistakes or things don’t go to plan.
Through collaboration our children learn from each other. They learn how to communicate effectively and to appreciate the views and needs of others.
We encourage our children to aim high, challenge themselves and to believe that they can accomplish anything that they put their minds to.
We develop children's independence so that they are able to make decisions and take responsibility for their success.

Southsea Ship Captains
Our school captains play a vital role in fostering a positive and inclusive school environment. They act as representatives of their peers, ensuring that their voices are heard and their concerns are addressed.
We believe that being a school council member provides valuable leadership and life skills, such as communication, teamwork, problem-solving, and decision-making. These skills are essential for personal growth and can empower children to become active and engaged citizens.

Support for Parents
Southsea Infants Home school link worker
Mr Hazlewood is our Home school link worker and acts as a supportive bridge between families and school, helping to ensure that parents are supported, and children are happy, settled and ready to learn. Mr Hazlewood is able to offer support, advice, or strategies for challenges like separation anxiety, emotional regulation, bedtime routines, or family stress (e.g., bereavement, separation, or financial strain). Mr Hazlewood is also able to signpost parents to external support networks, local food banks, parenting workshops, or health and social care services.
Dadzclub - in-person and online community building for father figuresPart of The Parenting Network, Dadzclub is a supportive community group where fathers can connect with each other and spend quality time with their children. The Dadzclub offer includes but is not limited to: Weekly Stay & Play sessions; Saturdays mornings at Buckland Family Hub and Monday evenings at the TPN Hub, The Bridge Centre, Fratton.A supportive Facebook group and educational social media presence, weekly football sessions and activities and events throughout the year. The team also works with organisations to raise awareness of health and parenting issues affecting men, redefining gender stereotypes and promoting discussions around gender equity.To learn more, visit the website www.dadzclub.com or email hello@dadzclub.com

A message from our Governors
We are pleased to welcome all parents and carers to Southsea Infant School. As a Governing Body we are immensely proud of our children and the school community, and we trust that your child will thrive in our learning environment. We have every reason to believe that their time at the school will be happy and rewarding.
As governors we endeavour to support Mrs Holmes and her staff as best we can by acting as ‘critical friends’ of the school. We are strongly committed to working in partnership with Mrs Holmes as effectively as possible in pursuit of the vision and agreed strategic direction for the continual improvement of our school. We take very seriously our responsibility as governors to monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of the school; and to hold the school to account for the standards achieved and for the quality of education provided.
You will find that that the school uses a range of ways to interact and communicate with parents/carers, and this is an area where the school will strive for further improvement. We believe that parents/carers are crucially important in the life of their child’s education, and you can certainly expect the school to facilitate your involvement in a whole variety of ways. Furthermore, as governors we are always keen to interact with parents through surveys, visits, and involvement in school events. We look forward to seeing and hearing from you.

Curriculum
At Southsea Infant School we offer a broad, balanced, relevant and engaging curriculum for all our pupils.
Our curriculum has been carefully constructed so that it is ambitious for all and takes into account the diversity of our school community.
We endeavour to enrich our children’s experiences, as well as build firm foundations in learning and personal growth whilst inspiring a life-long love of learning.
Our values of Perseverance, Aspiration, Collaboration and Independence are central to our approach in ensuring that our pupils are equipped with the fundamental skills that will allow them to become well-rounded, informed, active and valued members of the community and to lead happy, fulfilling lives.

Year 1 September 2026- Information for Parents
Y1 Phonics Information for Parents.
At the start of each half term, we will share our new learning plotters to give you a clear insight into your child's upcoming curriculum. Each plotter provides an overview of the term's topic alongside the core drivers shaping our learning. You will also find a breakdown of weekly learning expectations and the key vocabulary children will be introduced to throughout the unit, making it easier than ever to follow their progress and support their learning at home.
After consultation with teachers, governors and parents we have developed a new approach for 'home learning'. We have rebranded this as a menu of excitement! Year Teams will provide a new menu each half-term and the aim is for children and families to take the learning in whichever direction they would like. We have followed what a real menu looks like with the learning questions on the front and at the back some tasting notes- to give some guidance as to what the children could get up to! We hope you all enjoy it!
